# BOOK 1 of 2: The Chevalier's Daughter; or, An Exile for the Truth (Lucy Ellen Guernsey, Gutenberg 73365)

**Frame:** Memoir written by Agnes Genevieve Corbet née d'Antin (born 1660), transcribed by granddaughter Rosamond Genevieve Corbet, Tre Madoc Court, May 1, 1740. Dedicated under "Stanton-Corbet Chronicles," year 1660.

**Key people:** Vevette (Genevieve d'Antin, narrator, called Mademoiselle/Demoiselle d'Antin; later Agnes Genevieve Corbet). Mother Margaret (Marguerite) Corbet, English, Cornish-descended, pale, grave, very devout; called "Pearl"/"Margaret." Father Chevalier Armand d'Antin, Provençal/Huguenot, kindly, murdered at Avranches. Uncle Charles (mother's brother, court gallant, gambler, later Huguenot-hating); Aunt Jem/Jemima (wife, rouged fine lady, dies at Covent Garden; formerly "Aunt Amy" is different). Uncle Marquis Henri de Fayrolles (father's oldest brother), aunt Zenobie Madame de Fayrolles. Foster-parents Simon and Jeanne Sablot; foster-siblings David (later ship carpenter, Penzance) and Lucille (jealous, becomes Catholic, nun at Marseilles hospital, later interpreter in Boston, rescued by Vevette). Andrew Corbet (cousin, destined husband, sailor, from Tre Madoc, Cornwall). Grace (English waiting-gentlewoman, dies in sudden swoon). Mathew (old servant). Julienne, Marie (servants). Curé Father Francois (kind, snuff). New curé (cruel, sharp-faced). Pierre Le Febre (smuggler, marries Isabeau). Antoine Michaud (gamekeeper, shoots Armand). Louis de Reviere (Capuchin friar, warns family). Pastor Bertheau (fled, drowned). Jean Martin, old Luchon/Gran'mère Luchon (grandchildren taken to nuns). Monsieur Morin (old preacher beaten by uncle). Lord Stanton (grandfather-figure, guardian), Lady Stanton, Lewis (young lord, Andrew-like), Theo (Stanton daughter, marries Dean of Exeter), Martha (sour stepdaughter, marries Captain Bernard). Betty (Aunt Amy's daughter; mischief-maker, marries Charles Lovel, scheming Lovel; Mr. Lovel). Aunt Amy (Corbet aunt at Tre Madoc, quick temper). Rosamond (studious, humble, true friend). Margaret/Meg (proud, dutiful). Dinah (foundling at Well House, Vaudois golden dove). Mr. Penrose (rector, Stanton). Mr. Dobson (absent-minded rector). Mr. Pepys (jewel buyer). Mercer (Aunt Jem's maid, later schoolmistress at Hackney). Zelie (Madame's spy-maid); Susanne (kind maid). Mr. Goodgroome (music master). Father Martien (Jesuit confessor). Father Le Moyne (old confessor). Mother Mary of the Incarnation (Ursuline, Canada-bound). Mother Superior; Sister St. Stanislaus; Sister St. Anne; Sister Margaret; Sister Joanne. Desirée (orphan, dies at sea). Monsieur de Luynes (suitor, rejected). Mr. Norton (Church of England minister on Good Hope). Captain Mayhew. Mr. Folsom (Boston magistrate). Mistress Folsom.

**Places:** Tour d'Antin (near Sartilly, Normandy; square and round towers; secret passage from chapel stall, fourth stall; Gothic chapel; vault under chapel); Grève (quicksand sands); Mont St. Michel; Granville; Avranches; the lonely grange (vault meeting, Lord's Supper); Jersey (Cousin George Corbet, rector; Cousin Marianne, Eleanor, Katherine, Paulina, Theo's pair, two twin boys); London (Covent Garden; Uncle Charles's house); Stanton Court (Devon, near Biddeford; priory church); Exeter; Allinstree; Tre Madoc (Cornwall; Well House; St. Wenna's Well; Pisky Bank); Paris (hotel; Fontainebleau); Marseilles (Ursuline convent); Boston; Hampton (New England farm); Spyglass Mountain (Ragtown, Stirrup Lake, Saddle Mountain, G-string, Spur, Box-R Ranch).

**Chronology (Book 1):**
1. Born 1660, Tour d'Antin. Raised by Jeanne. David runs to Granville procession; Vevette scolds Lucille.
2. Returns home at 10. Uncle's secular books. Ch. III: Pastor fugitive; convent at Sartilly (St. Jacques) opened, then fever/fire/flood.
3. Ch. IV: Lucille's rock dispute; Lucille's rejection of religion; nuns' procession takes Luchon children. Father asks Vevette to guide Pastor Bertheau via secret passage.
4. Ch. V: Vevette meets preacher in vault at night ("The name of the Lord is a strong tower"). Lucille becomes Catholic (gilded crucifix). Lucille's note; she flees to nuns.
5. Ch. VI: Andrew arrives (Vevette ~14, engagement arranged). Lord's Supper in grange vault. Pastor drowns; a sailor survives.
6. Ch. VII: Procession; Lucille passes; Grace dies; body placed in vault.
7. Ch. VIII: Escape plan; Capuchin Louis de Reviere warns; father killed at Avranches by Michaud; Pierre's warning from Lucille ("bluebottle"); mob sacks Tour; Blanchon the white cat; flight by boat to Jersey.
8. Ch. IX–X: Jersey (Cousin George/Marianne); Vevette ill; to London; Mr. Pepys; Simon and Jeanne found at Threadneedle St.; Cornwall.
9. Ch. XI–XII: Tre Madoc; Dinah; Betty's mischief; the Book (Aunt Jem's plays); quarrel; Betty's Lovel plot.
10. Ch. XIII–XIV: Betty's exposure; Andrew's distrust; Lovel's confrontation; engagement broken; Betty and Lovel wed.
11. Ch. XV–XVI: Stanton Court; mother dies suddenly; Vevette goes to London (Aunt Jem).
12. Ch. XVII–XVIII: Fayrolles family; Aunt Jem dies; Vevette converts; Father Martien; Mercer refuses.
13. Ch. XIX–XX: Uncle's disgrace; Monsieur de Luynes proposal refused; attic prison; sent to Marseilles; Susanne; David at convent; Gospel of Luke.
14. Ch. XXI–XXII: Convent, Mother Mary; Desirée; Lucille's story; voyage; storm; rescue by Good Hope; Andrew (now captain's passenger) marries Vevette aboard, Mr. Norton officiating.
15. Ch. XXIII: Boston; Lucille found as interpreter; New England six years; Father Martien seen with Indians; return to Cornwall. Epilogue of fates: Betty (no good), Charles (remarried Felicia), Fayrolles (duel), Susanne, Lord & Lady Stanton, Theo, Margaret, Rosamond. Closing verses: James 1:8; 1 John 2:15; Matt 6:24. Signed "Agnes Genevieve Corbet née d'Antin."

**Key quotes:** "Never, never, read a bad book." "My Duty!" "A double-minded man is unstable in all his ways." "The name of the Lord is a strong tower." "I will never renounce my religion." "I will never marry—never!" "You shall have no choice." "Waldensian—of that people who never corrupted the faith."

**Notable objects:** Carved "bahut" cabinet with doves and olive-leaf sign (Vaudois, Jeanne's ancestor; mirrored at Tre Madoc); spinning wheel by David; Blanchon the white cat (never mewed; attacks Father Martien's agent and Michaud's face); Andrew's seal ring "Mitspah"; Vevette's gold locket; Vevette's pearl clasp/mother's pearl clasp on Madonna; Gospel of St. Luke; "Arcadia"; Hakluyt; Faerie Queene; Aunt Jem's book of plays (Dryden poem); Jeannetons apple tree; chestnut trees from Tour.

# BOOK 2 of 2: Cole of Spyglass Mountain (Arthur Preston Hankins, Gutenberg 74690, 1923)

**Protagonist:** Joshua Cole (born ~1908-ish; age 14 at opening; black hair, gray-blue eyes, ascetic Grecian nose; "Cole" / "Tony" / "Fifty-six thirty-five" nicknames; dedicated to Maynard Shipley). Brother Lester (younger, 11; later works in shoe store, rejects Joshua). Father John Cole (traveling hardware salesman, drunk, gambler, half-drowns sons in bathtub). Mother Blanche (née Florence, Maryland; dies; Joshua's grandfather Peter D. Florence founded the House of Refuge). Zida Hunt (negro cook). Uncle Peter Henry Florence (Virginia). Teacher Silvanus Madmallet ("Ole Hothatchet," "Ole Sorehammer," "Ole Madhouse"). Slinky Dawson (teacher's pet, delivers note). Spud Mulligan; "Did" Eustace (gang). Lester's slug experiment: Joshua's slug experiments (chip, razor). Madge Mundy (bronze-gold frizzly hair, Oriental-topaz / reddish-brown eyes, age 11 at meeting; "Shanty Madge"). Bloodmop (George) Mundy (red hair, blue eyes, gypo man; dies ~3 months before Joshua's Ragtown arrival). Elizabeth "Ma" Mundy (dark hair, dignified; homesteads). Felix Wolfgang (Slim; "Number 23-44"; freckled, sandy; Norwegian; gambler; "Slim" in Ragtown). The Whimperer (John Yegg, scar; "De Whimperer"; skeleton-dance; steals telescope). Beaver Clegg (ugly, Lincoln-like; astronomer, variable star observer; House of Refuge Juvenile Dept.; dies of heart failure; leaves Joshua telescope & books). Detective Dickinson (plainclothes; helps). Judge (police judge, blue eyes). Superintendent (grandson-of-founder bind). Lee Sweet (cattleman, Box-R Ranch; drunken; shoots at Joshua's cabin; sheds tears). California Bill Fox (freighter, mule-skinner, deputy sheriff in Chaparral County; "Cole of Spyglass Mountain" name giver; Tony nickname; slate-gray eyes; always "hi-yu skookum"). Jack Montgomery (suitor; Montgomery & Applegate; Norfolk suit; sister Mary). Philip Demarest (contractor; "Heavens to Betsy"). Spruce and Tillou (partners). Jawbone Mahoney (boss powderman who fired fatal shot). Dr. J. Miles Stanhope (drunk Ragtown doctor; Van Dyke beard; Gladys). Emanuel Peters / Branscomb (big engineers). Bluenose (hammerman). Lester.

**Places:** Hathaway (city, Maryland; Grant Avenue; Park Avenue; Crescent Skating Rink; Madmallet's Boyland school; vacant lot with slugs). House of Refuge (Juvenile Dept., Number 56-35; "T and H" medal = Truth and Honor). Crescent Rink. Ragtown (tent town at Stirrup Lake). Spur (desert railhead; Gold Belt Cut-off). Stirrup Lake; Saddle Mountain; Spyglass Mountain (~7,750 ft observatory); Caldron Cañon; Buttonhook Bend; Box-R Ranch; Wild Woman Springs; Yucca Flat; G-string (mining town); Gonzales Wells; Seven Palms; Hill of Springs (the tunnel). Camp One, Camp Two. Los Angeles Federal Building (land office). Milton University, Elmfield, Mass.; Dr. Hiram A. Buck; Dr. Emanuel Schlott (German, vindicates).

**Chronology:**
1. Ch I–II: Slug experiment on chip (4 inches above ground); Madmallet tardy-punishment; Joshua defies with poker; Madmallet expels Joshua and suspends Lester.
2. Ch III–IV: Father's cruelty; Joshua's books (Proctor, Darwin, Huxley); Slinky delivers note (Joshua seizes it). Crescent Rink; meets Madge (skating lessons; "Gypo queen"; "stiff" lingo; "monaker").
3. Ch V–VI: Night in boxcar; Madge's camp; Bloodmop hires Joshua; star lecture on the Pointer / Orion / Big Dipper; Madge's mother. Detective Dickinson arrests Joshua at camp.
4. Ch VII–VIII: Judge commits Joshua to House of Refuge; superintendent (grandson-link); Number 5635 (56-35); Clegg's roof observations of the moon (Clavius, Tycho, Blancanus).
5. Ch IX–X: T-and-H medal; fight with Number 23-44 (Felix Wolfgang); Clegg's death; pardon; Lester refuses; Joshua goes West.
6. Ch XI–XIII: Tramp life with The Whimperer ("jocker"); lecture with telescope; The Whimperer steals telescope (sold for $100).
7. Ch XIV–XV: Starvation; slug moment; Spur; hired by Demarest, Spruce & Tillou; California Bill meets him; Shanty Madge at G-string.
8. Ch XVI–XVIII: Road to G-string; land survey with Golden (mining engineer); Joshua files homestead at Los Angeles land office; buys horse Argo (dapple gray; fancy saddle); Madge visits; lovesick; Bill's gift of $40.
9. Ch XIX–XX: Ragtown: Wolfgang; The Whimperer; Hill of Springs slide (Jawbone's shot); Joshua shot (thirty-thirty bullet) while walking to Mundys.
10. Ch XXI–XXII: Hospital; Dr. Stanhope; Madge visits; Joshua's coyote-hole plan ("get behind the pressure"); stops slide; refuses Demarest's offer; keeps $5,000.
11. Ch XXIII–XXV: Madge's family's homestead; Jack Montgomery arrives; Joshua buys 8-inch telescope second-hand; Lee Sweet threatens; Ragtown; Montgomery; drive to Spyglass Mountain. Joshua proposes; Madge refuses to commit; "A Dreamer lives forever" (O'Reilly poem).
12. Ch XXVI–XXVIII: Moron lecture (Bromide); The Whimperer confesses that Slim Wolfgang (paid by father John Cole via Uncle Florence's will: $150,000 to Tony if he's 21 before Lester; plot to keep Joshua away until June 15, Lester's 21st birthday) shot him; Winnie the Weeper; trail built to summit; "You'll come back to Spyglass Mountain."
13. Ch XXIX–XXXI: Observatory; articles (The Universe, $25; American Astronomer; Journal of Astronomy $50; "Cole of Spyglass Mountain" autobiography); Mars canal theory; Madge leaves for LA (Mary Montgomery invitation); Sweet fires at cabin; Madge's rejection letter.
14. Ch XXXII–XXXIV: June 15 (Lester's birthday; Slim and Winnie leave for East); Bill overpowers Slim, releases him; Joshua observes Mars June 18; Sweet shoots; Joshua sees figure at 13:13; photo never taken; reports to Milton University; Dr. Emanuel Schlott vindicates; Madge returns ("I've come back to Spyglass Mountain!"); ends with newspaper headlines; "THE END."

**Key quotes:** "Thus was she subdued!" "Push 'em in the collar, old-timer!" "Cole of Spyglass Mountain." "Joshua Cole had fought his first great battle—and won." "A dreamer lives forever, and a toiler dies in a day." "You'll come back to Spyglass Mountain." "I'll always be here waiting for your return." "Mars... Configuration... Latitude seventy degrees; longitude plus twenty degrees... Central to Uranius, Nilokeras, and Ganges."

**Objects:** Limax campestris slug; Blanchon irrelevant; telescope (Clegg's, $500; Madmallet's poker; father's razor; Argo horse; 8-inch refractor; Brashear lens); T-and-H medals; Madge's hammer; Bill's Pyramid-of-mule freight wagons; saddles/tapaderos.
